value.rationale: Final size is a canonical epidemic invariant, and the nonzero limit is surprising relative to arbitrarily strong transient suppression: cumulative susceptible infections still reach the classical herd-threshold depletion despite long delay. It answers an interpretable singular limit of the exact motivating model with a sharp exponentially small remainder, not merely a plotted peak.

final_claim: For the deterministic saturating-incidence SIR equations S′=−βSI/(1+εI), I′=βSI/(1+εI)−αI with S0,I0>0 and βS0>α, as ε→∞ the final susceptible level satisfies S∞=α/β−1/ε+O(ε q^(αε/β)) for every fixed α/(β S0)<q<1; in particular S∞→α/β and initially susceptible depletion→S0−α/β>0.
limitations: The asymptotic requires S0,I0>0, βS0>α and ε→∞ across deterministic trajectories.
